forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Turns the floor pattern into the exact maximal value.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every natural number n greater than 1, define H_n as the sum from k = 1 to n of 1 divided by k, and define f_n on real numbers by f_n(x) = floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (floor of k times x) divided by k. Then for every real number r with (n minus 1) divided by n less than or equal to r and r less than 1, it holds that f_n(r) equals H_n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all natural numbers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with (n-1)/n <= r and r < 1

payload.statement_nl: Let n > 1, define H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, and let f_n be defined by f_n(x) = floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k. If r is a real number with (n-1)/n <= r < 1, then f_n(r) = H_n - 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let n>1 and let r be real with (n-1)/n <= r < 1. We show that every floor term in the definition of f_n(r) is determined explicitly.

Fix k with 1 <= k <= n. From r >= (n-1)/n we get kr >= k(n-1)/n. Since k <= n, we have k(n-1)/n >= k-1. Also r < 1 implies kr < k. Therefore
k-1 <= kr < k.
Hence floor(k r) = k-1 for every k=1,2,...,n.

In particular, floor(nr)=n-1, and
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k r)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (k-1)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (1 - 1/k) = n - H_n,
where H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Therefore
f_n(r) = floor(nr) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k r)/k = (n-1) - (n - H_n) = H_n - 1.
This is exactly the desired identity.
result_payload.proof_summary: For r in [(n-1)/n,1), one has k-1 <= kr < k for every k=1,...,n, so floor(kr)=k-1. Substituting into the definition of f_n gives f_n(r)=H_n-1.
